payload.alternatives: Linting every commit in the PR in CI: rejected, because squash discards them and only the title survives on main. Linting bot PRs too, or loosening scope-enum / subject-case to let their titles pass: rejected, it would weaken the rules for humans to accommodate generated text. Keeping it as a documented convention only: rejected, that is the state that let the hook go untracked.
payload.rationale: CONTRIBUTING.md already says commitlint is mandatory, but the husky commit-msg hook was never tracked in git, so nothing enforced it. Merges are squash-only and the PR title becomes the commit that lands on main, so the PR title is what must be linted. Enforcement is therefore two pieces: .husky/commit-msg (runs commitlint on local commits) and the Commitlint workflow (lints the PR title). The CI check is for humans only: it is skipped when the PR author is dependabot[bot] or github-actions[bot] (release-please), because their titles are generated and fail the repo rules by design (Dependabot capitalises the subject; release-please uses a chore(main) scope outside scope-enum). The commitlint rules themselves are unchanged: scope-enum and header-max-length are not to be touched.
payload.title: Conventional Commits is enforced by tooling: a tracked commit-msg hook and a CI check on the PR title

payload.alternatives: Keeping 85: rejected, it does not catch regressions. Setting the JS floor to the local 87.77: rejected, CI is the reference and local varies with machine load. Setting it to 88.64 or 88.6: rejected, brittle, a single mutant flipping category fails CI. Lowering or removing the 99 branch floor: rejected, out of scope and the documented reason still holds.
payload.rationale: The old 85 floor sat well below reality, so a regression of ten-plus points would still pass. Measured on 2026-10-20 against main: Infection (PHP) kills 3196/3196 mutants, MSI 100 both locally and in CI. Stryker (JS) scores 88.64-88.69 in CI across the last 25 runs (217 survivors), but 87.77 locally on one machine (about 16 mutants land as survived locally and as timeout, which counts as detected, in CI). Per the rule to prefer the CI number, the JS floor is set from CI: 88, the integer part, because the CI score is 1747/1971 = 88.635 and a floor written as 88.64 would fail the very run that produced it. Consequence accepted: a local Stryker run on a slower or differently loaded machine can sit under 88 while CI passes. The branch coverage floor of 99 in packages/js/vitest.config.ts stays as it is; the comment there explains the unreachable branches.
payload.title: Mutation score floors rise to what the project reaches today: Infection 100, Stryker 88; branch coverage floor stays at 99

payload.alternatives: Adopting vitest 5 and lowering or disabling the Stryker break threshold: rejected, a ~8% score means mutation testing stops testing anything. Closing the PRs without a config change (or with '@dependabot ignore this major version'): rejected, a plain close only skips that one version, and a comment-based ignore lives in Dependabot's own state where it cannot be reviewed or removed from the repo. Pinning vitest in package.json: rejected, it hides the hold from Dependabot instead of declaring it where it can be lifted. Leaving vitest in the generic npm group: rejected, that group would take vitest minor/patch bumps and could split vitest from @vitest/*.
payload.rationale: Stryker's vitest runner has an open bug on Vitest 5: the per-test name filter matches nothing (testNamePattern now joins the chain with ' > '), so every covered mutant survives (stryker-mutator/stryker-js #6210, open on 2026-10-20). On Dependabot's vitest 5 PR the CI mutation score fell from 88.6 to 8.07 (159 of 1971 mutants killed). @vitest/coverage-v8 5 on its own also fails against vitest 4, since the two ship in lockstep. So: the two Dependabot PRs (#93, #94) were closed with a comment citing the bug; .github/dependabot.yml ignores semver-major updates of vitest and @vitest/*, and groups vitest and @vitest/* in one group so they come back in a single PR. The group is listed before the npm group because Dependabot assigns a dependency to the first group that matches. To lift the hold: when stryker-js #6210 is fixed and released, delete the two ignore entries (the group can stay).
payload.title: Vitest 5 is held back until Stryker's vitest runner supports it; vitest and @vitest/* update together

payload.text: ADR-3 says the `vitest` group is listed before `npm` because Dependabot assigns a dependency to the first group that matches. That is wrong. Dependabot's job log (2026-10-21, after #101 merged) says "Skipping @vitest/coverage-v8 for group 'vitest' - belongs to more specific group 'npm'" and "Skipping vitest in group vitest as it has already been handled by a previous group": overlapping groups are resolved by specificity, and `npm` (dependency-type + update-types) outranks the pattern-only `vitest` group regardless of file order. Observed effect: vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 4.1.12 both landed in the `npm` group (PR #102), so minor/patch bumps still travel together, but not in a PR of their own. The `vitest` group only catches what `npm` excludes, i.e. majors, so the pair should still come back together once the major ignore is lifted (not observed yet, the ignore hides it). The decision itself stands: the major ignore works (vitest stayed on 4.x, no 5.x PR was recreated) and vitest and @vitest/* still move as a pair. Only the ordering rationale is superseded by this note.
payload.topic: Correction: Dependabot resolves group overlap by specificity, not file order
